scenario: LSER.10.9: `direction` is the sign of newest - previous over the two newest samples in the window, decided by comparison, and `null` with fewer than two. Drives the companion read `s.direction` of a `sliding` declaration -- the compiler routes it to the raw-sample backing (SeriesBackendRingBuffer) -- into libds's `ds_series_ring_buffer_direction` and Mercury's `aggregate(agg_direction)`. A `ttl` schema, so an equal value is still a sample (LSER.7.6.3). Row k: 10, 30, 20, 20, then a fifth assert; reads pre-sample (LSER.8.6.1): cold, then [10] null (no log), [10, 30] +1, [10, 30, 20] -1 (the newest pair falls, where the sign of rate first-to-last is +1), [10, 30, 20, 20] 0. Row w: -1, INT64_MAX, then a third assert; [-1, INT64_MAX] reads +1. THE `where` READS A SERIES, SO IT IS RE-READ EVERY PUMP ([LTIM.2.4.1]) and each live fact fires once, on the pump its condition first holds ([LTIM.2.5.1]): the two k facts before the third read +1 with it, so `k 1` logs three times, and the two w facts before the third likewise log `w 1`. A fact that has fired does not fire again while its direction stays non-null, whatever its value.
rules_ds:
use default

schema Sample scope ttl 1_d:
    dev: String
    level: Int

series Sample.level (by: dev):
    direction sliding 1_h

rule r:
    Sample s where s.direction is not null
->
    log info "{s.dev} {s.direction}"
